title: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition: Operational Guide (2026)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This operational guide consolidates Redwood Inference's core procedures for annual budgeting & forecasting, procurement and contracting, and revenue recognition/billing for fiscal operations. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, and product/engineering managers who participate in budget cycles, vendor selection, contract review, or billing operations.

Purpose:
- Standardize processes to reduce cycle time and control spend.
- Ensure compliance with contract governance and ASC606 revenue recognition principles.
- Provide clear owner responsibilities and escalation paths.

Scope:
- Applies to all corporate and product teams that request budget, purchase goods/services, execute contracts, or generate revenue-bearing agreements.
- Excludes personal reimbursement policies (see expenses policy) and capital asset accounting for fixed assets (see fixed-assets policy).

Key contacts and ownership:
- Finance (Budget Owner): Finance Director, Marcus Lee (marcus.lee@redwood.ai) — overall budget cadence and forecasting tool ownership.
- Procurement & Vendor Mgmt: Procurement Lead, Sofia Ramirez (sofia.ramirez@redwood.ai) — vendor onboarding, PO issuance, supplier performance.
- Legal (Contract Review): Senior Counsel, Daniela Kim (daniela.kim@redwood.ai) — contract review, signature authority confirmation, NDAs.
- Billing & RevRec: Revenue Accounting Manager, Liam O'Connor (liam.oconnor@redwood.ai) — invoicing cadence and recognition entries.

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (annual + rolling forecast)

1.1 Timeline and cadence:
1. Annual budget kickoff: first week of October.
2. Draft budgets submitted by team owners: by November 15.
3. Finance consolidation and leadership review: Nov 16 – Dec 10.
4. Final sign-off and allocation: Dec 20.
5. Quarterly re-forecast (rolling 12 months): end of each quarter (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec).

1.2 Inputs and templates:
- Use the official Budget Workbook (Finance/GDrive: /finance/budget-templates/2026-budget-master.xlsx).
- Required inputs: headcount plan (FTEs), run-rate infra costs (GPU hours by workload), SaaS subscriptions, professional services, capital requests (> $50k).
- Forecast types: Best case, Baseline (required), and Downside. Provide drivers and assumptions for each.

1.3 Ownership & approval rules:
- Team PM/Manager: prepares line-item requests and rationale.
- Finance Business Partner: validates assumptions and GL mapping.
- Final budget approvals: VP of Product (product spend), VP Engineering (infra & SRE), CFO (company-level).

1.4 Sizing and scenario guidance (examples):
- GPU capacity: assume 10% overhead for burst capacity and 3% monthly growth baseline for model-serving.
- Headcount cost: use standardized salary bands (see HR compensation workbook) plus 30% burden for benefits and taxes.

2) Procurement & Contracts (operational flow)

2.1 High-level procurement flow:
1. Requester submits Purchase Requisition (PR) in Procurement Portal with business justification and budget code.
2. Procurement team validates vendor and pricing; issues PO if approved.
3. Contracts requiring legal review routed to Legal via Contract Intake form.
4. On execution, Procurement confirms PO/contract countersigned and closes PR.

2.2 Purchase thresholds & approval matrix:
| Amount (USD) | Required Approvals | Notes |
|---:|---|---|
| <= 5,000 | Manager (budget owner) | Auto-approve in portal if budget available |
| 5,001 - 50,000 | Manager + Finance BP | Procurement involvement required |
| 50,001 - 250,000 | Director (owner) + Finance Director | Procurement lead reviews supplier terms |
| > 250,000 | VP level + CFO sign-off | Enterprise procurement and Legal mandatory |

2.3 Contracting workflow and SLAs:
- Standard NDAs and MSAs should use Redwood's approved templates (Repo: /legal/templates).
- SLA: Legal acknowledges intake within 2 business days, first review comments within 7 business days for standard contracts; larger/complex (non-standard clauses) may take 3–6 weeks.
- Procurement SLA: POs for approved requests issued within 3 business days of approved PR.

2.4 Contract review checklist (required items for Legal review):
- Counterparty legal name and entity paperwork.
- Term and renewal language (auto-renewal requires explicit opt-out).
- Pricing, payment terms (Net30 default), and invoicing instructions.
- Data protection clauses (if data processing involved): include DPA or refer to Redwood's standard DPA.
- IP assignment/licensing and reverse engineered outputs clauses.
- Limitation of liability and indemnity: ensure caps align with finance-legal policy (standard is 2x annual fee; deviations need CFO approval).
- Termination & transition assistance obligations.
- Audit rights and subcontractor flow-downs.

2.5 Approved vendors & procurement exceptions:
- Procurement maintains an Approved Vendor List (AVL) updated quarterly. AVL includes primary cloud providers, managed services partners, and hardware suppliers.
- Exceptions for new vendors require vendor risk assessment and AML/ sanctions screening.

2.6 Payment terms & remittance:
- Standard vendor payment term: Net30. Early payment discounts must be approved by Finance Director.
- Wire transfers and ACH require dual-signature confirmation for amounts > $50k.

3) Revenue Recognition & Billing (revrec & invoicing)

3.1 Revenue types and recognition principles (summary)
- Subscription (hosted API): recognized ratably over the subscription period (monthly) unless a separate performance obligation exists.
- Usage-based billing (tokens/embeddings): recognized as services are delivered (point-in-time recognition tied to metering period).
- Dedicated/Reserved capacity contracts (annual commitments): allocate to performance obligations; recognize ratably unless acceptance criteria indicate point delivery.
- Professional services (implementation): recognize over time if client simultaneously receives and consumes benefits; otherwise recognize upon completion/milestone.

3.2 ASC606 checklist (operational):
1. Identify contract(s) with a customer.
2. Identify performance obligations.
3. Determine transaction price (including variable consideration – discounts, rebates).
4. Allocate transaction price to performance obligations.
5. Recognize revenue as performance obligations satisfied.

3.3 Invoicing cadence and procedures:
- Standard SaaS billing: monthly arrears for usage; customers on prepaid subscriptions billed upfront and revenue deferred.
- Invoicing SLA: Finance issues invoices within 5 business days following the meter period close.
- Dispute handling: if customer disputes invoice, ticket created in Billing Queue and Finance responds within 3 business days; disputes resolved within 30 days.

3.4 Deferred revenue and journal entries (examples):
- Invoice for annual prepaid subscription $120,000 on Jan 1 (GL: 2000 Deferred Revenue). Monthly recognition journal on last day of each month: DR 2000 Deferred Revenue $10,000; CR 4000 Subscription Revenue $10,000.
- Usage invoice realized on month end: DR 1100 Accounts Receivable; CR 4100 Usage Revenue; collect per payment terms.

3.5 Billing exceptions & credits:
- Credits require manager approval and Finance review (credit memo workflow in Billing System).
- System refunds > $5,000 require CFO approval.

4) Controls, Auditability, and Record Retention
- Contracts and executed POs are stored in Contract Repository (DocuSign/SharePoint canonical location).
- Retention: contracts and revenue supporting documents retained for a minimum of 7 years.
- Monthly close checklist includes sample testing of deferred revenue roll-forward and AR aging review.

5) Operational KPIs & Targets
- Budget cycle time (kickoff to sign-off): target <= 8 weeks.
- PO turnaround (approved PR -> PO issued): target <= 3 business days.
- Legal review first pass SLA: acknowledge < 2 business days; first comments < 7 business days.
- Invoice issuance SLA: < 5 business days after meter close.
- AR collection: DSO target <= 45 days.

6) Escalation paths and exceptions
- Procurement disputes escalated to Procurement Lead (S. Ramirez) then to CFO for unresolved > 10 business days.
- Contract deviations from standard terms require Legal & Finance written exceptions, reviewed at monthly Contract Review Board.

7) Appendices & Templates
- Templates (links): MSA template, Standard NDA, DPA, Vendor Onboarding Form, Budget Workbook template.
- GL mapping quick reference:
| Business Area | Revenue GL | Example Account Code |
|---|---|---|
| Subscription | Subscription Revenue | 4000 |
| Usage | Usage Revenue | 4100 |
| Marketplace / Professional Services | Service Revenue | 4200 |
| COGS - Infrastructure | Infrastructure COGS | 5000 |

- Sample journal entry templates (text files in Finance repo).

Change history:

- 2026-01-12: Updated procurement thresholds and PO SLA (reviewers: M. Lee, S. Ramirez).
- 2026-02-15: Clarified revenue recognition examples for reserved capacity contracts.

summary: Operational guidance combining budgeting cycles, procurement & contracting flow, and revenue recognition / billing policies for 2026 fiscal operations.
